Create a resource by name.

A project registers the git repository at --path in the current group, which must exist unless it is the default group. A group is created empty and holds the projects you register with --group later.

Use --dry-run=client to check the arguments without writing anything, and -o yaml with it to print the manifest instead, ready for apply -f.

Resource types: projects (project, proj) and groups (group). Type words are case-insensitive.

Examples:
  # Register the repository at ~/dev/hldr as a project in the current group
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr'

  # Register a project in the work group with two labels
  slipway create project api --path '~/work/api' -n work --label lang=go --label tier=api

  # Register a project with the remote and the branch it is expected to have
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr' --remote git@github.com:hvpaiva/hldr.git --branch main

  # Create a group with a description
  slipway create group work --description "Projects for the day job"

  # Check the arguments without writing the project
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr' --dry-run=client

  # Print the manifest of a project without registering it
  slipway create project hldr --path '~/dev/hldr' --dry-run=client -o yaml

Options:
      --path DIR           Directory of the git repository to register; required for projects. A relative directory is stored resolved against the current directory, a ~ path as written.
      --description TEXT   A short description of the resource.
      --label KEY=VALUE    A label to set on the new resource; may be repeated.
      --remote URL         The URL the origin remote is expected to have, written to spec.remote. A URL that embeds credentials is refused; use a credential helper.
      --branch NAME        The branch the project is expected to have checked out, written to spec.branch.
      --dry-run STRATEGY   Only print what would change, without writing anything, when the strategy is client. One of: none, client. (default "none")
  -o, --output FORMAT      Output format; without it, each resource prints a result line such as project/hldr created. One of: json, yaml, name.

Usage:
  slipway create TYPE NAME [flags]

Use "slipway --help" for a list of global options (applies to all commands).
